description: Cross-slice integration (issues #689 Sound + #680 Interaction & Events, saga #572 M5): a single program running `set_tempo`, `beep`, `wait`, and `beep` together proves the two profiles share one deterministic, headless execution event stream (spec/conformance.md#sound: Sound "may share the execution event stream with Interaction & Events"). Each statement emits its `instruction` event first, then its effect event in program order: `sound` AFTER sound state is scheduled (spec/interaction-events.md#trace-stream-integration) and `primitive` (name: wait) AFTER the pause completes (spec/interaction-events.md's `### wait <n>`). No tick count, tempo-read, or wall-clock timing leaks into any payload (headless; spec/execution-model.md's trace-and-event registry). This fixture guards the rebase resolution that placed both the sound scheduler and the tick clock on one `Environment`, confirming they coexist rather than merely existing side by side. M5 adds no new event kind: `sound` and the `primitive` catch-all are both registered by C5 (#694).
